messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Customer: Polaris Systems | region: ap-southeast-1 | resource: dedicated-pool/polaris-apac-pool | symptom: p99 latency 2.8s (SLO 800ms) | auto-page @Ravi Singh
Ravi Singh: oncall here, taking lead. Quick ask: is this affecting only tenant polaris or noisy neighbor?
Claire Huang: I'm pulling tenant partition metrics. Early read: polaris traffic normal QPS, but we see sustained cpu async queue backlog on pool workers and KV miss rate jump to 60%. A small subset of tenant-ids from Polaris are causing very large prefix requests (~4x normal tokens).
Nate Fox: Joining war room, starting real-time tracing. Opening zoom: https://zoom.redwood/w/incident-pol-22
Olga Petrov: Paging infra to validate node health. `redwood nodes list --pool polaris-apac-pool` -> node-a, node-b, node-c (primary), node-d (hot spare). node-b shows 99% GPU util and rising memory footprints.
CSM-Polaris: Notified Polaris Systems support + engineering. They're seeing customer batch job running at 03:40 local, may be expected but not announced. Asking them to pause if possible.
Ravi Singh: Immediate mitigation candidates: 1) tenant isolation (route offending tenant to isolated small pool), 2) emergency per-tenant throttles at edge, 3) spin new hot-spares locally, 4) fallback to smaller model (v2-small) for that tenant, 5) cross-region drain to ap-southeast-2. Which two should we parallelize?
Claire Huang: Start tenant isolation and throttle in parallel. Isolation minimizes blast radius and keeps other tenants unharmed. I'll check compatibility for model fallback.
Nate Fox: Kicking off isolation: `redwood tenant isolate --tenant polaris-tenant-77 --from-pool polaris-apac-pool --to-pool polaris-apac-sandbox --preserve-kv=true` -> starting, estimated 90s.
infra-ops-bot: Tenant isolation workflow started. Provisioning sandbox nodes: sand-1, sand-2.
Ravi Singh: Applying emergency throttle while isolation proceeds: `redwood route update --tenant polaris-tenant-77 --qps 20 --window 60s --reason "protect pool stability"`
Nate Fox: Throttle applied. Observing p95 from 1.2s -> 560ms in next 60s. p99 from 2.8s -> 1.4s. Good immediate effect.
Claire Huang: Isolation completed. Offending tenant now on sandbox pool. Observed that requests are heavier (token count median 3.9x). KV miss rate for sandbox still high; maybe prefix variance means cache cold.
Olga Petrov: Sandbox nodes healthy but provisioning logs show cold-start artifact for model loads with longer initialization on node sand-1. Recommending warmup script: `redwood warmup --pool polaris-apac-sandbox --model v2-quant`
Ravi Singh: CSM-Polaris, request you to confirm stopping the batch or throttling on your side while we stabilize — we can provide gradual ramp steps.
CSM-Polaris: Customer acknowledged. They will pause the job for 5 minutes and coordinate with their infra team.
Claire Huang: Next step: get a short-term model fallback for that tenant to v2-small which has known lower memory usage. I validated that v2-small supports current prompt schema; slight latency improvement but lower throughput per GPU.
Nate Fox: Initiating fallback: `redwood routing set --tenant polaris-tenant-77 --model v2-small --reason "memory-stability mitigation"` -> applied.
Ravi Singh: After isolation, throttle, and model fallback: p95 now 430ms, p99 780ms (within SLO). Error rate unchanged.
Olga Petrov: Noted a pattern of large batched requests originating from a handful of IPs from the customer's CIDR. Recommend we enforce connection-level concurrency caps and add a tenant-specific prefix cache warm layer.
Claire Huang: I'll prepare a follow-up recommendation: cache-warm policies + token batching guidance + model selection guidance. Also collecting heap dumps from node-b pre-restart: `redwood trace collect --node node-b --duration 90s --output /tmp/polaris-nodeb-heap.pb`
infra-ops-bot: A node-restart request is queued for node-b to clear any stuck GC state. Manual approval required for dedicated pools.
Ravi Singh: Approving restart under incident authority. Proceed with rolling restart on node-b (drain -> restart -> uncordon).
Nate Fox: node-b drained and restarted. Post-restart memory stabilized; no immediate OOM. p99 remains ~770-800ms.
CSM-Polaris: Posting customer update: "We've applied temporary throttling for the impacted workload, isolated the heavy tenant to a sandbox pool, and applied a model fallback. We've paused the customer's batch job and are monitoring. We'll share RCA and next steps shortly."
Ravi Singh: Incident status: mitigated but active monitoring needed for 30 minutes. Actions assigned: Ravi -> incident timeline and postmortem, Claire -> RCA drafts and heap analysis, Nate -> implement cache-warm runbook and check sandbox perf, Olga -> confirm node restart telemetry and autoscale approvals. CSM -> coordinate customer comms and collect whether they will change batch cadence.
Nate Fox: One more note: consider adding a per-tenant burst token bucket enforcement in routing layer so future sudden batch jobs can't degrade pool. Filing follow-up ticket: INF-5421.
Olga Petrov: PagerDuty handoff in 20 minutes to next oncall (Claire). I'll ensure all logs and traces are uploaded to the incident doc.
Claire Huang: Taking handoff. Will keep thread open and update incident doc with timelines and preliminary impact numbers.
Ravi Singh: Thanks all. Leaving thread open for 1 hour then will set to post-incident review. Great coordinated response :thumbsup:
